references.text: The basic command that everything that first opens the womb belongs to the Lord, both of humans and animals.
The regulation for redeeming firstborn humans and unclean animals, especially the donkey as an example of an unclean animal.
Explanation of why the firstborn must be redeemed or sacrificed - in remembrance of when the Lord struck down all the firstborn in Egypt.
Law that the firstborn of sons and livestock are to be given to the Lord.
Repetition of the law that everything firstborn belongs to the Lord, and that donkeys and firstborn sons must be redeemed.
The Lord's claim on all firstborn from the day he struck down all the firstborn in Egypt.
Practical example of redemption money for the Israelite firstborns who exceeded the number of Levites.
Next verse specifying the redemption price: five shekels of silver when the child is one month old.
Regulation concerning firstborn animals and the redemption of unclean animals with an additional fifth.
Jesus is presented in the temple in Jerusalem as a firstborn son, in accordance with Mosaic law that every male firstborn shall be consecrated to the Lord.
